title: Employee Guidelines for Dealing in Securities

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: The collective defined term: all directors and Key Management Personnel, the Leadership Team, all employees and contractors of Peet or any related body corporate or managed syndicate, and their associates.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: All directors and key management personnel (as defined in the ASX Listing Rules) of Peet or any related body corporate or managed syndicate; must follow the section 2.3 notification procedure for any proposed dealing at all times and face a stricter, Board-determined standard to trade outside the window.

tiers.name: Leadership Team
tiers.description: The leadership team of Peet, as determined from time to time; subject to the same section 2.3 procedure as Key Management Personnel (notifying the Managing Director and Group Company Secretary) but not necessarily KMP under the Listing Rules.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of Peet, including the Managing Director; must notify the Chairman and Group Company Secretary before any transaction and complete an ASX Appendix B-style memorandum for Listing Rule 3.19A change-of-interest reporting.

definitions.hedging_definition: schemes ... that specifically protect the value of unvested shares, options and performance rights granted under any equity-based remuneration plans

windows.start_anchor: holding of the Annual General Meeting

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Peet may notify an individual Employee, during a window, that they may not buy or sell during all or part of it because Peet possesses price sensitive information (2.1(b)); confidentiality of such a notification is not addressed. There is no separate mechanism for the Board to impose additional blackout periods generally.

rules.detail: No express rule on dealing in derivatives generally. Securities extends to 'items relating to securities issued by Peet (for example, warrants and other derivative products)', and Dealing includes entering into an agreement to buy or sell. Employees may deal freely (including in such products) during the 60-day windows if not in possession of inside information; outside the windows, dealing is prohibited unless cleared by the Managing Director. It is unclear whether a bespoke OTC product issued by a bank (rather than 'issued by Peet') falls within this Securities definition at all.
rules.evidence: Securities ... also extends to items relating to securities issued by Peet (for example, warrants and other derivative products).

rules.detail: Absolute ban on schemes that specifically protect the value of unvested shares, options and performance rights under an equity-based remuneration plan. Not framed as a 'holding lock' concept; the guidelines do not otherwise distinguish a vested-but-restricted state.
rules.evidence: It is a condition of these guidelines that no schemes are entered into by any Employee that specifically protects the value of unvested shares, options and performance rights granted under any equity-based remuneration plans.

rules.detail: Section 2.7's hedging ban only reaches unvested shares, options and performance rights. Hedging of vested securities is not named and is caught only as ordinary dealing under the window/clearance regime.
rules.evidence: any dealings in securities acquired upon exercise of options or performance rights must only occur in accordance with these guidelines.

rules.detail: Not named. A prepaid forward or similar arrangement is an 'agreement to subscribe for, buy or sell securities' and so dealing, permitted in a window (absent inside information) or outside a window with Managing Director clearance; if it protects the value of unvested securities it would also breach 2.7.
rules.evidence: enter into an agreement to subscribe for, buy or sell, securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the guidelines.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the guidelines.

CFDs are not named. As a 'derivative product' referencing Peet securities, a CFD is a Security and dealing in it requires window/clearance compliance; it would also ordinarily be an 'other short term dealing' requiring Managing Director approval under 2.4.
rules.evidence: Employees may not enter into any other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts) except with the approval of the Managing Director.

rules.detail: Margin loans are not mentioned anywhere in the guidelines.
Granting security, a charge or a lien over securities is not mentioned and is not within the Dealing definition (buy/sell, agreement to buy or sell, exercising an option).

No provision addresses margin loans or any other secured financing arrangement in respect of Peet securities; the Dealing definition (buy/sell, agreement to buy or sell, exercising an option) does not obviously extend to granting security to a lender.

Buying and selling securities within a three month period, and other short-term dealings such as forward contracts, are prohibited unless the Managing Director approves (special hardship carve-out for the buy/sell rule).
rules.evidence: Employees may not deal in Peet's securities on a 'short-swing' basis, except in circumstances of special hardship, with the Managing Director's approval. That is, Employees may not buy and sell securities within a three month period. In addition, Employees may not enter into any other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts) except with the approval of the Managing Director.

clearance.evidence: dealing in Peet's securities outside of the 'window' period is prohibited, unless Employees receive clearance by informing and receiving approval from the Managing Director prior to undertaking a transaction ... It is intended that a request to trade outside of the 'window' period will be answered within 48 hours.

clearance.approver: Chairman and Group Company Secretary (director); Managing Director and Group Company Secretary (Leadership Team); Board or next most senior director and Group Company Secretary (Chairman)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: director completes Appendix B memorandum on the trade; Company Secretary must notify ASX of a director's notifiable interest change within 5 business days (Listing Rule 3.19A)
clearance.evidence: At all times, Key Management Personnel and the Leadership Team must follow the procedure below for any proposed dealing in Peet's securities on the ASX: a director of Peet (including the Managing Director) must notify the Chairman and Group Company Secretary prior to undertaking a transaction.

short_term.basis: from acquisition (buy and sell within the period)
carve_outs: circumstances of special hardship, with the Managing Director's approval
short_term.evidence: Employees may not deal in Peet's securities on a 'short-swing' basis, except in circumstances of special hardship, with the Managing Director's approval. That is, Employees may not buy and sell securities within a three month period.

exceptions.evidence: transfers of securities of Peet already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Employee is a beneficiary.

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of Peet) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party.

where an Employee is a trustee, trading in the securities of Peet by that trust provided the Employee is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade outside of a 'window' is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Employee.
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer.

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board of Peet.

such other transfers of securities as are determined by the Board not to be restricted, having regard to Corporations Act, the Listing Rules and the need to ensure there is no perception that any Employee is trading in securities whilst in possession of inside price sensitive information.

Exceptional circumstances in which Key Management Personnel and the Leadership Team may be permitted to buy or sell Peet's securities may include severe financial hardship ... The Board may require the person requesting to trade to provide evidence to satisfy the Board that they are in severe financial hardship and that the proposed trade is the only reasonable course of action available.
Employees may not deal in Peet's securities on a 'short-swing' basis, except in circumstances of special hardship, with the Managing Director's approval.
court order requiring the sale of the securities.

certain passive trades ... or when the company has announced such information ahead of the complete release of half yearly results or annual results as to result in the Board being satisfied that there is no price sensitive information about Peet that is not generally available and that there will not be a perception that any trading by Key Management Personnel and the Leadership Team is on the basis of price sensitive inside information.

exemption_authority: The Board determines whether exceptional circumstances (hardship, certain passive trades, court order, or a Board-satisfied pre-results information carve-out) justify approving Key Management Personnel or Leadership Team trading outside a window (2.3); the Managing Director approves ordinary Employee trading outside a window (2.2) and hardship exceptions to the short-term dealing ban (2.4). No exemption authority is stated for the section 2.7 hedging ban on unvested securities.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The guidelines contain no provision on margin loans, security interests, charges or any other financing arrangement in respect of Peet securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A loan secured on the collared shares is not expressly regulated, and granting security is arguably outside the Dealing definition (buy/sell, agreement to buy or sell, exercising an option) altogether, so the loan leg may fall wholly outside this policy's clearance and window requirements - a benefit for structuring, but also a source of legal uncertainty since no process, disclosure or forced-sale carve-out is provided if the bank ever needs to enforce.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to unvested securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: no schemes are entered into by any Employee that specifically protects the value of unvested shares, options and performance rights granted under any equity-based remuneration plans.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar can be written over vested shares without breaching 2.7, since the ban does not reach vested holdings or a 'holding lock' concept, which this policy does not use.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees may buy or sell Peet's securities on the ASX in the period of 60 days commencing immediately following the announcement of half-yearly results, annual results, or the AGM ... dealing in Peet's securities outside of the 'window' period is prohibited, unless Employees receive clearance.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike a typical blackout-period model, trading is closed by default and only opens in three 60-day windows a year (or with Managing Director clearance outside them), so collar inception and any physical settlement should be timed to a window or separately cleared.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Unless there are exceptional circumstances, approval will not be given to enable Key Management Personnel and the Leadership Team to trade in Peet's securities outside the 'windows'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For KMP and Leadership Team participants the Board applies a materially stricter standard than the Managing Director's approval available to other Employees, so collar execution or unwind for this tier should be planned within a window wherever possible.

bespoke_clauses.topic: ambiguous scope of 'Securities' for bank-issued OTC derivatives
bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities ... also extends to items relating to securities issued by Peet (for example, warrants and other derivative products).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The extension is framed around instruments 'issued by Peet'; it is unclear whether a bespoke bilateral OTC put/call issued by a bank (not by Peet) referencing Peet shares is 'Securities' under this policy at all, though the general insider trading law prohibition on dealing in 'securities' would still apply independently.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Policy Number: RMP03. Version 5. Revised 12 August 2015.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only version of the policy lodged in the dataset and is over a decade old with no evident amendments addressing derivatives, CFDs, short selling, securities lending or financing; the bank should confirm no newer, unlodged version exists before relying on its silence on these topics.

summary: A funded OTC equity collar looks structurally achievable under this policy for vested, unrestricted shares, and the secured-loan leg appears to sit entirely outside its scope. The put and call are dealt with only as ordinary 'dealing in securities': Employees may transact freely (absent inside information) during the three 60-day windows following half-year results, annual results or the AGM, or at any other time with prior written clearance from the Managing Director (answered within 48 hours); Key Management Personnel and the Leadership Team must additionally notify the Chairman/Managing Director and Group Company Secretary before any transaction and face a much stricter, Board-determined standard to trade outside a window. Section 2.7's absolute hedging ban is limited to unvested shares, options and performance rights, so it does not reach a collar over vested holdings. The guidelines are entirely silent on margin loans, encumbrances or any other secured financing arrangement, so the loan secured on the collared shares is not expressly regulated or prohibited - likely because granting security is not itself 'dealing in securities' under this policy's narrow definition - though that silence also means no process exists for financier disclosure or a forced-sale carve-out if the bank later needs to enforce. The three-month short-term dealing ban (with a Managing Director hardship carve-out) should be factored into collar tenor and any early unwind timing.
